# Illustration

One of the PLUS illustration characters: a textured body with a face, arms and legs in line work. It is decorative unless given a `title`.

**Import:** `import { Illustration } from '@/components';`

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/images-and-icons/Illustration/Illustration.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/images-and-icons/Illustration/Illustration.stories.jsx` — Gallery, SmartCharacters, MathCharacters, Sizes, DefaultSize, Rest, Decorative, Titled, MasteringContent, Advocacy, Technology, Relationships, SocialEmotional, Dot, ApproximatelyEqual, Root, All, Pi, Equal, Divider, Interactive

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/images-and-icons/Illustration/Illustration.mdx`

## Usage

Use `Illustration` to give a page or a moment some warmth: the header of Home,
an empty state, a welcome, or a card that introduces a SMART area. A character
is decoration beside words that already say what the page is about.

Use an icon, not a character, for anything a person acts on or has to read to
understand. Use `Tile` for a small square picture of a thing.

When to use a character, which one and how it sits on a page are on
Illustrations. This
page is the component's API.

## Best practices

### Pick a SMART character for a SMART area, and a math character for anything else. {#pick-a-smart-character-for-a-smart-area-and-a-math-character-for-anything-else}

Do: A SMART character for its area; a math character for the rest.
Don't: A math character standing in for a SMART area.

### Keep characters decorative unless they carry meaning. {#keep-characters-decorative-unless-they-carry-meaning}

Do: Decorative beside a heading that already says it.
Don't: A title that repeats the heading, so it is read twice.

### Don't crop a character. {#don-t-crop-a-character}

Do: Give it room.
Don't: Clipping the box cuts off the limbs.

## Accessibility

- **Decorative by default.** Without a `title` a character is hidden from
  assistive technology (`aria-hidden="true"`), since it sits beside words that
  already say what the page is about.
- **`title` makes it one image with a name.** The character becomes
  `role="img"` with that name, and its parts stay hidden, so it is announced
  once. Give it a title only when it carries meaning on its own.
- **The line ratio is a property of the source art.** The line work measures
  about 2.6:1 on the bodies in Light and about 2.7:1 in Dark. That is under 3:1,
  and it is fine for decoration, which has no contrast requirement. Never put
  information in a character that a person needs to read.
- **Every mode.** Bodies and line work take their colors from tokens alone, so
  a character follows Light, Dark and increased contrast with nothing to set.

## Parts

1. **Frame.** The square layout box, `size` wide and high. The limbs reach past it and are never clipped.
2. **Body.** The textured shape, filled from a body token and masked by the stipple.
3. **Line work.** The face, arms and legs, in one icon token.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | The only state. A character is a picture, not a control. |
| Hovered, pressed, focused | None. Wrap the character in a button or link that carries the name and the focus. |
| Disabled | None. Dim the control around it. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Body, SMART characters | The area's `subtle` background, such as `--ds-background-smart-advocacy-subtle`. |
| Body, math characters | An accent `subtle` background: red, blue, green or purple. |
| Line work | `--ds-icon-subtle` |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Title a character that stands alone with what it stands for: "Advocacy". | Title it "Illustration" or "Character", which names the picture. |
| Leave the title off a character beside a heading that says it. | Repeat the heading in both places. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `character` | oneOf | `'mastering-content'` | Which character. The first five are the SMART areas; the rest are math characters. |
| `size` | number | `96` | The frame's width and height in pixels: 48, 96, 160 or 240, or any number. Limbs reach past it. |
| `title` | string | — | Makes the character an image with this name. Without it the character is decorative and hidden. |
| `className` | string | `''` | Extra class names added to the character's frame element beside the component's own. |
| `style` | object | — | Inline styles for the frame element. They are applied after its width and height, so they can override `size`. |
